survivingClaim: CLASSICAL (Rouche step of Bagchi's criterion; not new): for a zero with gamma_0 > 0 the number of one-separated Rouche returns is R(T) <= N(beta_0 - r, T + gamma_0 + 1). So power-sparse recurrence at every hypothetical off-line zero (exponent 0.2308 at beta_0 = 7/8, tending to 1 as beta_0 -> 1/2) is equivalent to RH. For a hypothetical zeta zero the return set has frequency 0 and every finite Bohr set leaves the zero in the tail R_P. MEASURED (float64): DH has 8116 zeros in 0.52 <= Re s <= 1.2 up to 1e5; returns at positive rate at three DH zeros (fraction 1.0e-4 to 4.3e-4 at r = 0.1), within 13 to 17 percent of a Haar Monte Carlo model.
obstruction: A recurrence hypothesis whose returns each produce a zero is bounded by the zero count, so it is as strong as the zero-free statement (restatement). zeta_P never vanishes, so an off-line zeta zero is a Haar-null event carried by the tail beyond every finite prime set; Kronecker equidistribution gives frequencies only for sets of positive Haar measure. Closed at step 2.
controlsThatDefeat: sign twist: not separated (argued, not proved)
DH and E_a: separated only through the density estimate, not through the recurrence step
lesson: Reject combinations whose amplifier is 'one zero implies many zeros' via Bohr sets or almost periodicity.
